 Order

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C') has been filed by the petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 519/2015, registered at Police Station Vikas Puri, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Manoj Pant, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Ms. Meena Sehrawat and Investigating Officer (IO) Inspector Kuldeep Singh from Police Station Vikaspuri,
Delhi.

4. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 had been solemnized on 19.10.2013 according to Hindu rites and customs at Alwar, Rajasthan and out of this wedlock, one female child was born on 30.10.2014.
It is stated that due to several temperamental differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no.2, they started living separately.

On 11.07.2014, the respondent no. 2 filed a complaint against the petitioners at CAW Cell, Kirti Nagar, which was converted to FIR bearing no. 519/2015, registered at Police Station Vikas Puri, Delhi for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC.
It is further stated that petitioners and respondent no. 2 have settled all their disputes amicably on 22.12.2018 before Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi on 22.12.2018 and learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that affidavit showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court has been filed and the same is on record.
6.

entities.text: Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

7. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 29,00,000/- in three instalments in the following manner:
a. First instalment of Rs. 7,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement in first motion petition.
b. Second instalment of Rs. 7,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement in second motion petition.
c. Third/final instalment of Rs. 15,00,000/- to be paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of quashing of FIR before Hon'ble High Court at New Delhi.
8.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 15,00,000/- today, i.e., 22.03.2023 vide DD No. 302576 for a sum of Rs.
5,00,000/- and DD no. 302577 for a sum of Rs. 10,00,000/- both drawn on State Bank of India,
New Delhi, and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 519/2015, registered at Police Station Vikas Puri, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. The present petition stands disposed of.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MARCH 22, 2023/
